requires: Owner approval on 2026-11-12; synthetic tests passing; SHA-256 recorded in the run script before any score is computed
question: On the public outputs of Wang and Ji's BART model and Jo et al.'s T5 version, does N-way retrieval hold within one corpus, or only when movie reviews and biographies are mixed?

inputs.eeg: None. No EEG file is opened and nothing is trained
inputs.primary_output: Free generation from each model's plain file
inputs.noise_output: BART intput_noise file. For T5 the EEG_noise file, read as trained on EEG and tested on noise; the README does not define the name
inputs.teacher_forced: Secondary only. These outputs are conditioned on the target text

corpus_labels.biography: Target matches a normal-reading sentence in the local ZuCo 1.0 or 2.0 manifests, by squashed text or token Jaccard of at least 0.7
corpus_labels.validation: Compare with the task labels in GLIM's local CSV files wherever a target appears in both. Only 6 of 104 sentences do, so this is a weak check
corpus_labels.expected: Wang and Ji hold out about 10% of each task: roughly 40 movie reviews and 65 biographies

protected.policy: Targets matching a v1 test sentence, a v2 test block or its buffer, by squashed text or token Jaccard of at least 0.7, are removed before scoring

evaluation.primary: Expected 10-way top-1 by cosine between each output and the pool of unique test sentences, computed exactly from ranks, ties are misses, averaged within sentence and then across sentences; chance 10%
secondary: Corpus label only, no EEG: the mean text of the other test sentences in the query's corpus
Number of distinct outputs and share of rows taken by the most common one
Teacher-forced outputs and the other noise files, scored the same way

decision_rule.bootstrap: 10000 resamples of per-sentence scores, two-sided 95% intervals. Readers cannot be resampled, as the files carry no reader labels
decision_rule.clear: Gap at least the minimum and the lower bound above 0
decision_rule.mixed: Each sentence against all scored sentences
decision_rule.within_corpus: Each sentence against the other scored sentences of its own corpus, one equal weight per sentence
decision_rule.beats: Clear of chance and clear of the noise arm on the same pool

outcomes.condition: Mixed pool does not beat chance and noise
outcomes.label: No retrieval above chance or noise in these outputs

outcomes.condition: Mixed pool beats both, and the within-corpus score does not
outcomes.label: The mixed score comes mostly from telling the corpora apart

outcomes.condition: Mixed pool beats both, and so does the within-corpus score
outcomes.label: The score holds within a corpus

decision_rule.secondary_scope: Secondary results never change the label

refuse_if: A file's size or SHA-256 differs from this plan
The files of one model list different targets, apart from the BART 7_22 file
Any corpus label by elimination disagrees with a GLIM task label
A scored target matches a protected sentence
Row, sentence or corpus counts differ from this plan
audit.false_pass_check: Before freezing, on synthetic outputs over 20 seeds each: random outputs, corpus-only outputs and sentence-level outputs earned the first, second and third labels on 20 of 20

test_policy: No final test data is scored. These are other authors' public outputs
stop_rule: Stop after this run whatever the outcome. No extra files, embeddings or settings under this plan.
existing_output_policy: Refuse to run if the output directory exists; hash protected prior artifacts before and after

cohort.use: Sentence text only, to label corpora and to find protected sentences

files.left_out: The four task1_task2_task3 files in the T5 repository. Their task-specific sentences cannot be told from movie reviews with local lists
